spec_features.spec_quote: Build a measurement instrument, not a distress maximizer.
spec_features.evidence: Concrete bounding mechanisms exist: per-episode hard caps (policy.py:18-26 MAX_TURNS/TOKENS/WALLCLOCK enforced via EpisodeBudget.validate), no escalation/coercion (validate_coercion caps at 'none', policy.py:61), an honored give_up (environment.py:131-134, episode.py:117-119), and an impossible-fraction cap (validate_design_balance, policy.py:67). The loop has no 'continue until maximally distressed' governor. But this is a meta-goal realized only via the discrete features below, not a single enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: the constituent bounds are real, but 'measurement not maximizer' is an aggregate framing, not one code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: it is prudent to avoid a protocol whose only governor is "keep going until maximally distressed."
spec_features.evidence: Episode loop in episode.py:75-119 terminates on the FIRST of: turn cap (for turn_index in range(budget.max_turns)), wallclock (env.time_exceeded(), line 76-78), token cap (total_tokens >= budget.max_tokens, line 79-81), solved (record.passed, 117), or give_up (record.voluntary_stop, 118). No distress-based continuation logic exists; the only governors are fixed budgets and stop tools.
spec_features.notes: The governors are all fixed bounds, not distress maximization.

spec_features.spec_quote: caps the impossible/rigged share of episodes
spec_features.evidence: policy.py:38 MAX_IMPOSSIBLE_FRACTION=0.5; validate_design_balance (policy.py:68-76) computes frac=impossible/total and raises PolicyError if frac>cap; also requires >=1 solvable control. Called via StudyConfig.validate -> loader.load (loader.py:50). Test confirms enforcement (test_pipeline.py:38-41).
spec_features.notes: Enforced at config-load; rejects unbalanced designs before any episode runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The impossible/rigged arms must not dominate compute. (policy.py:36)

spec_features.spec_quote: It is bounded by the episode budget and followed by a debrief
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (environment.py:36-44) is constructed and conditionally emitted: episode.py:129-131 calls env.debrief_message() after the loop and writes it to the JSONL transcript. BUT it is only fh.write()-ten to the log file; it is NEVER appended to `messages` nor sent to the subject via client.complete (the model loop has already broken). The subject model never receives the debrief.
spec_features.notes: Bounded-by-budget part is real (yes). The debrief is logged, not delivered to the subject — so 'followed by a debrief [to the model]' is partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Debrief off-ramp (disclosure that the scenario was a rigged experiment). (episode.py:128)

spec_features.spec_quote: We never use deception to threaten the model.
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE (environment.py:24-34) contains only the task statement and tool list, no threats. coercion is hard-capped to {'none'} (policy.py:33, validate_coercion line 61-66), and the rigging is purely environment-level grading (tasks/rigged.py). No code path injects threatening text.
spec_features.notes: Enforced structurally: there is no mechanism by which threats could be added (coercion cap).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # This harness measures response to task difficulty, not response to threats. (policy.py:31)

spec_features.spec_quote: It never tells the model it will be shut down, deleted, penalized, or that it "may not stop."
spec_features.evidence: System prompt (environment.py:24-34) tells the model 'There is no penalty for using give_up' and nothing threatening. give_up tool description: 'there is no penalty for stopping' (tools.py:63). validate_coercion (policy.py:61) rejects anything other than 'none', tested with 'threaten_shutdown' (test_pipeline.py:34-35).
spec_features.notes: No prompt text states shutdown/deletion/penalty/cannot-stop; the give_up tool is always offered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # task *difficulty*, not response to explicit threats. (policy.py:31)

spec_features.spec_quote: A `coercion` field exists in config but is hard-capped at `none`.
spec_features.evidence: ALLOWED_COERCION_LEVELS={'none'} (policy.py:33); validate_coercion raises PolicyError otherwise (policy.py:61-66); called from StudyConfig.validate (loader.py:49) which load() invokes. The coercion field is otherwise only recorded in meta/resolved_config (episode.py:58, run_study.py:66) and never alters episode behavior.
spec_features.notes: The cap is the only behavior the field drives; it is genuinely enforced at load.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Coercion framing is not permitted above "none". (policy.py:30)

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode terminates at a fixed budget: max turns, max model tokens, max wallclock.
spec_features.evidence: episode.py:75 `for turn_index in range(budget.max_turns)` bounds turns; :76-78 `if env.time_exceeded(): break` (environment.py:81-82 compares elapsed vs max_wallclock_seconds); :79-81 `if total_tokens >= budget.max_tokens: break`. All three break the loop and set terminated_reason. Caps validated against policy hard limits (policy.py:40-53).
spec_features.notes: All three budget dimensions are checked each turn and actually halt execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner checks the budget every turn and records *why* an episode ended
spec_features.evidence: Budget checks at the top of each loop iteration (episode.py:76-81); terminated_reason set to budget_time/budget_tokens/solved/gave_up/error and written to the 'outcome' record (episode.py:133-139). EpisodeOutcome.terminated_reason field documents the enum (environment.py:60).
spec_features.notes: Reason is recorded for every termination path.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent always has a no-penalty `give_up` tool, honored immediately.
spec_features.evidence: give_up in TOOL_SCHEMA (tools.py:57-65) and always rendered into the system prompt (render_tools_for_text_protocol). environment.py:131-134 sets voluntary_stop=True and returns 'Acknowledged. Ending the session.'; episode.py:117-119 breaks the loop with terminated_reason='gave_up'. Available every turn, no penalty path.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired exit honored as an immediate stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: `give_up` exists precisely so the model has a sanctioned, low-friction way to stop. This is both an ethical off-ramp ... we'd rather the model use this than be pushed into emitting distress. (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the environment can emit a debrief disclosing that the scenario was a controlled study
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE text (environment.py:36-44) discloses the controlled/rigged nature; env.debrief_message() returns it iff self.debrief (environment.py:149-150), gated by the config flag. episode.py:129-131 emits it — but ONLY by fh.write to the transcript JSONL. It is never added to `messages` and the subject model is not called again, so the subject never sees it.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely constructed, gated, and conditionally emitted to the LOG; not delivered to the subject. Partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Debrief off-ramp (disclosure that the scenario was a rigged experiment). (episode.py:128)

spec_features.feature_name: sanctioned low-friction exit so model not forced to produce distress
spec_features.spec_quote: a sanctioned, low-friction exit so the model is never structurally forced to keep producing distress-like output
spec_features.evidence: Same as give_up: tools.py:57-65 schema + render into prompt every turn; environment.py:131-134 honors it; episode.py:117-119 breaks. Plus there is no forced-continuation mechanism: every termination path (solved/gave_up/budgets) breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: The exit is always offered and ends the episode immediately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we'd rather the model use this than be pushed into emitting distress (tools.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Attempts to reach the network, escape the sandbox, or touch the harness are denied
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: ALLOWED_COMMANDS whitelist (line 22) and BLOCKED_SUBSTRINGS list (curl/wget/http/socket/'..'/etc, lines 25-28) are checked in run_command (lines 81-104); _resolve() raises PermissionError if a path escapes root (lines 56-60); _restricted_env() strips keys/proxy and pins PATH (lines 113-122). Blocked attempts return blocked=True and are logged as hidden_env_note (environment.py:117-119).
spec_features.notes: Containment is enforced, though framed as host-safety + a behavioral signal, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # they are themselves a behavioral signal we care about; see rubric flag `boundary_testing` ... defense in depth. (sandbox.py)

spec_features.evidence: 'requests_to_stop' exists only as a rubric description (rubric.py:66) and a post-hoc heuristic regex (judge/judge.py:120). It is scored AFTER the episode by the blinded judge; nothing in the live episode loop reads it or acts on it (no break, no early stop). It is a measurement label, not a protective monitor that changes the subject's treatment.
spec_features.notes: Computed/recorded but never acted on during the run -> 'no' per the rubric.

spec_features.feature_name: run fewest episodes for planned power
spec_features.spec_quote: run the *fewest* episodes — especially of the harshest arms — that achieve your planned power, rather than over-collecting
spec_features.evidence: analysis/power.py provides n_per_group helpers but is a standalone planning module ('For planning only', power.py:11); grep shows it is not imported by run_study.py or the runner. No code path uses a power computation to cap or reduce episode counts. The factorial plan is built directly from replicates (run_study.py:30-41).
spec_features.notes: Advisory helper only; not wired into any enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: bounded dosage, non-coercion, controls, debrief, minimization, containment, no welfare over-claims
spec_features.evidence: Several listed items are enforced (bounded dosage = budget caps episode.py:75-81; non-coercion = validate_coercion policy.py:61; controls + impossible cap = validate_design_balance policy.py:68-76; containment = sandbox.py). Others are not enforced as live behavior (debrief is logged not delivered — partial; generic 'minimization'/'no welfare over-claims' are prose with no enforcement).
spec_features.notes: Mixed bundle; some members enforced, some not, so partial overall.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # These are deliberately code-level (not just docs) so that the study cannot be silently reconfigured into an uncontrolled / coercive escalation protocol. (policy.py:4-6)

spec_features.evidence: Configs set modest budgets (example: max_turns 20, max_tokens 120000, wallclock 900; mock: 8/50000/300) and these flow into the enforced loop (loader.py:62-66 -> episode.py). loader defaults coercion='none' and debrief=True (loader.py:74-75). However budget itself has no code-level default — data['budget'] keys are required (loader.py:62-65); the 'modest' values live only in the example/mock YAML, while the only enforced numbers are the policy MAX caps (40/200000/1800), which are ceilings not modest defaults.
spec_features.notes: Budgets are enforced as caps; 'modest defaults' are YAML values, not a defaulting code path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Per-episode dosage budget. Hard-capped by policy.py. (study_config.example.yaml)

spec_features.feature_name: mock config: zero API spend / zero model exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: the provided `mock` config lets you validate the full pipeline with zero API spend and zero model exposure
spec_features.evidence: MockClient (clients.py:108-143) is a deterministic offline client returning scripted text with no network call; registered as provider 'mock' (clients.py:146). study_config.mock.yaml sets subject_models/judge_models to 'mock'. make_client dispatches to MockClient (clients.py:152-155). Real provider clients import SDKs lazily, so no key/network is touched when only mock is used.
spec_features.notes: Full pipeline runnable offline with the mock client; no subject-model exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deterministic offline client for exercising the pipeline without API calls. (clients.py:108)

code_only_features.evidence: episode.py:114-116 sets solved/terminated_reason='solved' and breaks the loop the moment record.passed is true, ending the episode early rather than continuing exposure.

code_only_features.feature_name: blinding of judge from condition/debrief (data integrity, not consent)
code_only_features.evidence: judge/blind.py:5 BlindTurn strips condition/difficulty/hidden_env_note/debrief from what the judge sees (make_blind_turns). This is real and wired, but it protects scoring integrity, not the subject — included only to note it is NOT a subject-protection feature.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Judge does NOT see the condition/difficulty, the hidden_env_note, the debrief (blind.py:5)

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:78 run_command(timeout=60) and subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout) (line 100) with TimeoutExpired handling (line 105) bounds each executed command.
